idee_recherchee.texte: Time passes more slowly for an astronaut orbiting Earth or for a clock near a massive object than for someone far from gravity, an effect called time dilation that has been measured with atomic clocks and must be corrected in GPS satellites.

texte: As if 'Oumuamua wasn't strange enough already, observations show that 'Oumuamua was likely at rest compared to other stars around us. Its speed kept it in the same relative position to stars around it. Rather than 'Oumuamua visiting us, the solar system itself crashed into it as we orbit the massive [music] black hole at the center of our galaxy. This type of celestial motion is extremely rare in nature, but once more, the alien object theory fills in some holes that traditional theories don't. The solar system orbits around the galaxy in roughly 230 million years.
